generation.hypothesis: The presence of ferromagnetic ground states in high-entropy alloys can be determined using the substitution of ferromagnetic elements with antiferromagnetic elements, which introduces positive enthalpies of mixing and creates miscibility gaps.
generation.intervention: Substitution of ferromagnetic elements with antiferromagnetic elements
generation.mechanism: Introduction of positive enthalpies of mixing
generation.boundary: Temperature and composition of the alloy
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of how the substitution of ferromagnetic elements with antiferromagnetic elements affects the presence of ferromagnetic ground states is not fully understood

cited_evidence.text: Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: Substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr introduces positive enthalpies of mixing (Fe-Cr, Co-Cr, Ni-Cr), creating miscibility gaps that strongly enhance the tendency for B2 phase decomposition.. System: AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi high entropy alloy. Conditions: Annealed at 600 °C and 1000 °C for 15 h. Evidence: inferred. Observation: The addition of Cr caused a strong tendency for phase separation into B2 + BCC even at 1000 °C, unlike the Cr-free alloy.. Scope limits: The mechanism does not apply to the Al-Cr binary system which has a propensity for compound formation due to negative enthalpy of mixing.. Alternatives: The authors considered that the phase separation is introduced by Cr, distinct from the behavior of AlCoFeNi.. Quote: "The strong tendency of Cr to introduce phase separation in the B2 phase can possibly be attributed to a positive enthalpy of mixing of Fe-Cr, Co-Cr and Ni-Cr systems"
